name: self-heal-loop
context: Agent systems where a deterministic verifier evaluates the output of each execution step and triggers a repair-retry cycle when the output fails validation. Unlike reflexion (which uses verbal learning from failure feedback), self-heal-loop uses a programmatic verifier — a test suite, schema validator, or policy check — to drive the repair, enabling fully automated correction without human or LLM-generated critique.
benefits: Fully automated error correction without human intervention
Deterministic verifier provides objective pass/fail signal
Catches regressions that LLM self-critique might miss
Each iteration moves closer to a verifiable end state
tradeoffs: Requires a deterministic evaluator — not all failure modes are programmatically checkable
Can loop indefinitely if the verifier is mis-specified
Repair may introduce new errors between verification cycles
Higher per-attempt cost than single-pass when failures are rare
use_cases: Code generation: an agent writes a function; a test suite runs; failures trigger targeted repair
Data pipeline: outputs are validated against a schema; invalid rows trigger regeneration with corrected constraints
API responses: JSON output is validated against a schema; malformed responses are regenerated
Infrastructure as code: a plan is applied to a dry-run environment; drift detection triggers correction
avoid_when: No deterministic way to evaluate whether the output is correct
The task is inherently subjective (creative writing, opinions)
Failures are so rare that the overhead of the loop is not justified
technology_stack: LangGraph while loop with validator nodes
Claude Agent SDK with built-in verify tool
anti_patterns: Verifier that always passes — the loop becomes an infinite generator
Repair that introduces a new error not caught by the verifier
No maximum iteration cap — runaway loops consume budget without converging
Failure drift: fix one error, introduce another
design_principles: The verifier must be objective and deterministic — same input always produces same result
Each repair must be targeted at the specific failure, not a wholesale regeneration
An iteration cap (step-budget) is mandatory to prevent infinite loops
Verifier must output: {location, observed_value, expected_alternatives, confidence}
best_practices: Design the verifier to be specific — catch only the failure class, not unrelated properties
Log each verify-repair cycle so failures are traceable to specific input conditions
Combine with agent-resumption so interrupted loops can resume from the last checkpoint
references: Dao et al., Agentic Design Patterns: A System-Theoretic Framework, 2026 — https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.19752
